rules.statement: Never set `TreatWarningsAsErrors` to `false` in any project or `Directory.Build.props`, test projects included; every maintained project is held to zero warnings.
rules.why: The rule is 'code we maintain', not 'code we ship'. A build that always prints warnings teaches people to stop reading them, which hides xunit.analyzers correctness findings and NU190x vulnerability advisories.
rules.check: Look for `TreatWarningsAsErrors` set to false, or removed, in any .csproj or Directory.Build.props/targets, especially under tests/.

rules.statement: Do not use a project-level `NoWarn` as a catch-all to silence warnings. Fix the code first. If a rule is noise for a whole tree (such as tests), add a per-rule `.editorconfig` entry with a one-line justification. For one isolated site, use a tight `#pragma warning disable`/`restore` pair with a reason.
rules.why: Making a relaxation name the rule and give a reason keeps the exception list auditable and reviewable, instead of hiding it in a disabled gate.
rules.check: Look for new `<NoWarn>` entries in project files, `.editorconfig` severity downgrades with no justification comment, and `#pragma warning disable` with no reason or no matching `restore`, or one that covers more than the offending lines.

rules.statement: When calling a method whose `out` parameter is annotated `[MaybeNullWhen(false)]`, declare the receiving local as nullable. In tests, narrow a maybe-null value with `Assert.NotNull(x)` before dereferencing it, rather than using `!` or a non-nullable local.
rules.why: This fixes nullable warnings (CS8600/CS8602) at the source instead of suppressing them, and it removes `null!` usages.
rules.check: Look for non-nullable locals receiving `[MaybeNullWhen(false)]` out arguments, and for maybe-null results dereferenced in tests without a prior `Assert.NotNull`.

rules.statement: Keep `IDE0005` (unused `using` directives) enabled at warning severity for test code too. If a test project would otherwise need `GenerateDocumentationFile=false`, set it to `true` and suppress `CS1591` instead.
rules.why: Roslyn only evaluates IDE0005 when documentation file generation is on, and raises a hard error otherwise. Unused usings rot in tests just as they do in production code.
rules.check: Look for changes that disable IDE0005 for tests, or that set `GenerateDocumentationFile` to false in test projects.

rules.statement: After running `dotnet format` (for example `dotnet format style --diagnostics IDE0005`), re-run CSharpier before committing.
rules.why: The .NET formatter and CSharpier can disagree about the resulting layout.
rules.check: Look for mechanical `dotnet format` diffs whose layout CSharpier would rewrite, such as formatting that is not CSharpier-normalized.
